content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes the quality checklist. **This is the first review gate** — please read it and confirm before I move on to planning. Nothing will be planned or built until you approve.

- **Spec:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all items pass, no open clarifications)

## What the spec says, in plain terms

**The app** — a personal web app to save and manage bookmarks.

**User stories (prioritised):**
- **P1 — Save a bookmark:** paste a web address; the app records it and auto-fills the page title when it can.
- **P1 — Browse & open:** see everything you've saved and click through to the original page.
- **P2 — Edit & delete:** fix a title/address or remove a bookmark (with a confirm step).
- **P3 — Find:** search by term and filter by tag once the collection grows.

The two P1 stories together are the minimum viable product.

**Key things it commits to:** address validation, auto-title (best effort), notes and tags, duplicate warning, persistence across restarts, empty/no-results states.

## Assumptions I made (please confirm or correct these)

These are the decisions that most shape the app. If any is wrong, tell me and I'll revise the spec before we plan:

1. **Single user, no login** — private personal app, no accounts or sharing.
2. **Web app for desktop browsers** — no mobile app or browser extension in v1.
3. **Local persistence** — no cross-device sync or cloud backup in v1.
4. **No import/export** from browsers or files in v1.
5. **Tags** are included (used for filtering); notes are a free-text field per bookmark.

## Your options at this gate

- **Approve** → I proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan, which you'll also review).
- **Change something** → I update the spec first.
- **Want me to sharpen any ambiguity with structured questions** → I can run `speckit-clarify`.

How would you like to proceed?
I approve the specification and the five assumptions. Please proceed to the implementation plan.

## The plan in plain terms

**Shape of the app:** one small web application — a single server that both serves the browser UI and answers a small JSON API, storing everything in a local database file on disk.

**The chosen approach and why:**
- **Node.js + Express server** — one `npm start` runs the whole thing; matches the review environment (port 4000).
- **Local SQLite database file** — survives restarts, no external service, fast enough for thousands of bookmarks. Fits your approved "local persistence" assumption.
- **Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript UI** — no heavy framework or build step, keeping it simple and quick to load. About four views: the list (with empty state), an add/edit form, search + tag filter, and a delete confirmation.
- **Best-effort title fetch** — when you don't type a title, the server briefly tries to read the page's title; if the page is slow or unreachable it falls back to the address and never blocks your save.
- **Address handling** — accepts `example.com` shorthand (adds `https://`), rejects genuine non-URLs, and warns (doesn't silently duplicate) when you re-save the same address.

**How correctness will be checked:** automated unit/API tests plus Playwright end-to-end tests covering all four user stories, described in the quickstart.

**Everything maps back to the spec** — no new behaviour was introduced beyond what you approved.

- **Change something** (e.g. a different technology, or you'd rather store data differently) → I revise the plan first.

## Task breakdown — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md`

**32 tasks across 7 phases**, organized so each user story is an independently testable increment.

| Phase | Focus | Tasks |
|-------|-------|-------|
| 1. Setup | Project structure, dependencies, config | T001–T003 |
| 2. Foundational | Database, URL helpers, title-fetch, server skeleton | T004–T008 |
| 3. US1 — Save a bookmark (P1) 🎯 | Validate/normalise/auto-title/dedupe + save UI | T009–T013 |
| 4. US2 — Browse & open (P1) | List newest-first, open in new tab, empty state | T014–T018 |
| 5. US3 — Edit & delete (P2) | Update/delete + confirm step | T019–T023 |
| 6. US4 — Search & tags (P3) | Search, tag filter, no-results state | T024–T028 |
| 7. Polish | Playwright e2e, truncation, harness config, full validation | T029–T032 |

**Per story:** US1 = 5 tasks, US2 = 5, US3 = 5, US4 = 5 (plus 3 setup, 5 foundational, 4 polish).

**Suggested MVP scope:** US1 + US2 (both P1) — save, browse, and open bookmarks end-to-end.

**Parallel opportunities:** foundational helpers (T005/T006/T008), the paired test tasks within each story, and whole stories split across people after Phase 2.

**Tests included** (per the approved plan): `node --test` unit/API tests per story, and Playwright 1.61.0 end-to-end tests covering the quickstart scenarios in Phase 7.

**Format check:** all 32 tasks use the required `- [ ] Txxx [P?] [Story?] description + file path` format.

## Next gate

Spec ✅ and plan ✅ are both approved — so we've cleared the gates that block implementation. Before I run `speckit-implement`, two quick options:

- **Approve tasks → I proceed to implement** against this breakdown (I'll build the MVP first: Setup → Foundational → US1 → US2, then continue through US3/US4 and polish).
- Optionally, I can first run **`speckit-analyze`** (a non-destructive consistency check across spec/plan/tasks) if you'd like an extra verification pass before building.

No `after_implement` hooks (no `.specify/extensions.yml`). Implementation is complete and validated.

## ✅ Implementation complete — Bookmark Manager

All 32 tasks done; **39 automated tests pass** (31 unit/API + 8 Playwright end-to-end covering every quickstart scenario), plus a manual smoke test confirming the API, static UI, and persistence across restart.

### What was built (against the approved spec/plan)
A single Node.js + Express app serving both the UI and a JSON API, backed by a local SQLite file.

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| Server + API routes | `src/server.js` |
| Data access & business rules | `src/bookmarks.js` |
| Storage/schema | `src/db.js` |
| URL validate/normalise/dedupe | `src/url.js` |
| Best-effort title fetch | `src/title-fetch.js` |
| Browser UI | `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `public/styles.css` |
| Tests | `tests/unit/`, `tests/api/`, `tests/e2e/` |

### User stories delivered
- **US1 Save** — validates/normalises the address (`example.com` → `https://example.com/`), auto-fetches the title when blank, warns on duplicates (with "save anyway").
- **US2 Browse & open** — newest-first list, opens in a new tab, empty state.
- **US3 Edit & delete** — edit form + delete with a required confirmation.
- **US4 Search & tags** — live search over title/address/notes/tags, tag filter, clearable no-results state.

### Two fidelity fixes made during implementation (spec unchanged)
Both were implementation defects caught by the tests, so I fixed the code against the spec rather than changing the spec:
1. Non-http schemes (`ftp:`, `javascript:`) now rejected with the correct message.
2. Timestamps keep millisecond precision so quick edits update `updated_at` correctly.

### Ready for your review
The harness is configured (`/work/.harness/app.json`, `npm start`, port 4000). The broker will launch it on demand — you'll reach it at **http://maker:4000**. The UI signals readiness via `data-harness-ready="true"` once the list/empty state loads.

Would you like to review it in the browser, or shall I adjust anything? If you spot behaviour you'd like changed, tell me which — I'll route it either as a fidelity fix (code only) or, if it's a spec change, back through `speckit-specify` and re-plan as our workflow requires.
This meets the approved behavior, and I accept the completed application.
